answer: Randomized honeypot audits resist sybils: the protocol secretly seeds planted bad answers — an opal among plain stones — and any grader who approves one is slashed. Because the beacon that picks the targets is unpredictable, a colluding ring cannot forge safe approvals in advance; they must judge honestly or risk the penalty on every call. This turns cheap rubber-stamping, the sybil's favorite tactic, into a losing gamble with real downside.
